name: AWS Data Sources
description: Connect to DynamoDB, S3, and other AWS services from the MicroVM using IAM role credentials.

cells.code:
import boto3
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# The MicroVM has an execution role with AWS credentials injected automatically.
# No keys to manage — just use boto3 directly.
session = boto3.Session(region_name='us-west-2')
sts = session.client('sts')
identity = sts.get_caller_identity()
print(f"MicroVM is running as: {identity['Arn']}")
print(f"Account: {identity['Account']}")

# Read sales data from S3
account = identity['Account']
bucket = f'microvm-sandbox-artifacts-{account}-us-west-2'

s3_client = session.client('s3')
obj = s3_client.get_object(Bucket=bucket, Key='samples/sales_data.csv')
sales = pd.read_csv(obj['Body'])
print(f"Loaded {len(sales)} orders from S3")
sales.head()

# Read product catalog from DynamoDB
dynamo = session.resource('dynamodb')
table = dynamo.Table('microvm-demo-data')
response = table.scan()
products = pd.DataFrame(response['Items'])

# Fix Decimal types
for col in ['price', 'stock', 'rating']:
    products[col] = products[col].astype(float)

print(f"Loaded {len(products)} products from DynamoDB")
products.sort_values('price', ascending=False)

# Merge: enrich sales data with product details from DynamoDB
# Sales has 'product' column, DynamoDB has 'name' column
# Create a mapping from product name to category and rating
product_map = products.set_index('name')[['category', 'rating', 'id']].to_dict('index')

# Map product names in sales to categories
sales['category'] = sales['product'].map(lambda p: product_map.get(p, {}).get('category', 'Unknown'))
sales['product_rating'] = sales['product'].map(lambda p: product_map.get(p, {}).get('rating', 0))

print("Sales enriched with DynamoDB product metadata:")
sales[['order_id', 'product', 'category', 'product_rating', 'quantity', 'unit_price']].head(10)

# Analyze: Revenue by product with DynamoDB ratings
sales['revenue'] = sales['quantity'] * sales['unit_price'] * (1 - sales['discount'])

product_summary = sales.groupby('product').agg(
    total_revenue=('revenue', 'sum'),
    total_orders=('order_id', 'count'),
    avg_quantity=('quantity', 'mean'),
    avg_discount=('discount', 'mean'),
    product_rating=('product_rating', 'first')
).round(2).sort_values('total_revenue', ascending=False)

print("Product Performance (S3 sales + DynamoDB ratings):")
product_summary

# Visualize: Revenue vs Rating scatter
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5))

# Revenue by product
colors = ['#89b4fa', '#a6e3a1', '#f9e2af', '#f38ba8', '#cba6f7']
axes[0].barh(product_summary.index, product_summary['total_revenue'], color=colors[:len(product_summary)])
axes[0].set_xlabel('Revenue ($)', color='#a6adc8')
axes[0].set_title('Total Revenue by Product', color='white', fontsize=13)
axes[0].tick_params(colors='#a6adc8')
axes[0].grid(axis='x', alpha=0.15)

# Revenue by region
region_rev = sales.groupby('region')['revenue'].sum().sort_values(ascending=False)
axes[1].pie(region_rev.values, labels=region_rev.index, autopct='%1.0f%%',
           colors=['#89b4fa', '#a6e3a1', '#f9e2af', '#f38ba8'],
           textprops={'color': '#cdd6f4', 'fontsize': 11})
axes[1].set_title('Revenue by Region', color='white', fontsize=13)

plt.suptitle('Sales Analytics (S3 data + DynamoDB enrichment)', color='white', fontsize=14, y=1.02)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# Time series: Monthly revenue trend from S3 data
sales['date'] = pd.to_datetime(sales['date'])
sales['month'] = sales['date'].dt.to_period('M').astype(str)

monthly = sales.groupby('month').agg(
    revenue=('revenue', 'sum'),
    orders=('order_id', 'count'),
    avg_order_value=('revenue', 'mean')
).round(2)

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 4))
plt.plot(monthly.index, monthly['revenue'], marker='o', linewidth=2, color='#89b4fa')
plt.fill_between(monthly.index, monthly['revenue'], alpha=0.1, color='#89b4fa')
plt.title('Monthly Revenue (from S3 sales data)', color='white', fontsize=14)
plt.xlabel('Month', color='#a6adc8')
plt.ylabel('Revenue ($)', color='#a6adc8')
plt.xticks(rotation=45, color='#a6adc8')
plt.yticks(color='#a6adc8')
plt.grid(alpha=0.15)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
